description: Fixed input shared by the Rust (ort+CPU/CoreML) and Swift (Core AI) bench sides. Shape mimics what vex's build_context() emits: module path + symbol name + signature, occasionally with a doc-snippet, varying in length up to the ~1100-char budget. Both MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim, ~22M) and jina-code (768-dim, ~117M) share this budget per vex's registry, so the same corpus exercises both models. Hand-crafted for stability across vex releases — DO NOT regenerate; results comparability depends on identical input.

src/parse/rust.rs::extract_rust uses tree-sitter-rust 0.24 SCM queries; for impl blocks captures both the impl target and any associated trait via (impl_item trait: (type_identifier) @trait)

src/index/rename_chains.rs::RenameChain v1.16 sidecar tracks symbol identity across renames via git-log --follow + similarity scoring; emitted alongside the main .vex blob and consumed by vex history --expand-renames

src/embed/extra.rs::FastEmbedModel wraps fastembed::TextEmbedding for non-MiniLM models in the registry (jina-code 768-dim, bge-small 384-dim, etc); see SPECS const for the full table including char_budget and gpu_auto_min_misses per model

src/search/fusion.rs::reciprocal_rank_fusion blends inverted-index hits, semantic-HNSW hits, and structural-AST hits via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) with per-source weight tuning; exact-name matches get a flat boost above the fusion to ensure they always rank first

src/store/format.rs::Header binary index header with magic VEXR, format version (currently v9), embedder_id, vector_dim, symbols_offset, bloom_offset, hnsw_offset, refs_offset, history_offset (added in v1.16.0 for the persistent history sidecar that ships as a separate .git_history file alongside the main .vex blob)

src/embed/integrity.rs::find_minilm_onnx walks the HF-Hub-style cache layout (models--Qdrant--all-MiniLM-L6-v2-onnx/snapshots/<commit>/model.onnx) to locate the ONNX bytes for SHA verification; returns None when fastembed cache layout has drifted, in which case the integrity check is skipped with a warning and the load proceeds so a fastembed upgrade doesn't break vex for everyone

src/cli/cmd_index.rs::run main indexing entrypoint: walks the project directory under gitignore rules, parses each file via tree-sitter, extracts symbols + refs, runs the cross-file resolver pass, optionally embeds symbol contexts via the resolved Embedder, builds the HNSW index, writes the .vex blob with manifest + bloom + inverted index + ref graph + (optionally) dense vectors + (in v1.16+) history sidecar, all under a single atomic rename at the end so partial writes never corrupt a working index

src/parse/python.rs::extract_python the Python extractor uses tree-sitter-python 0.25 queries to capture function_definition, class_definition, and decorated_definition nodes, with attention to nested classes (qualified names like Outer.Inner.method) and decorators that change visibility (e.g. @staticmethod, @classmethod); async def is treated as a regular function in the symbol table, with the async-ness recorded in the modifier bitset

src/search/semantic.rs::query_embed embeds a single query string at search time using the same Embedder ID that the index was built with (enforced by check_embedder_match at the reader boundary); on a CPU-only build the query embed is single-threaded and runs in ~10ms for MiniLM, on a GPU build it warms up the EP once per process and ~2ms thereafter, so query latency is dominated by the HNSW search itself for top-k <= 50 unless the index is cold-paged

src/store/reader.rs::IndexReader::open memory-maps the .vex file read-only via memmap2::Mmap::map, parses the Header, validates the magic + format-version + checksum, then constructs slot offsets for symbols / bloom / inverted index / HNSW / refs / history; lazy section access (each section is only touched on first query) means cold-open is fast (~3ms for a 50MB index on warm-cache filesystem) and the OS page cache effectively warms what the query touches

src/cli/cmd_status.rs::print_status walks the project's vex cache directory (resolved via xxh3 of canonical project path — see feedback_cache_path_writer_reader_symmetry for the on-disk path resolution rules), prints the index location, the manifest contents (embedder_id, vector_dim, build_timestamp, last_update), bloom stats, hnsw stats, history sidecar status (present / outdated / missing), and finally a one-line stats summary including symbol count, file count, and the rename_chains count if v1.16+ history sidecar is present

src/history/scoring.rs::score_rename uses a weighted blend of edit-distance on the body tokens (40%), signature shape similarity computed via Jaccard on the parameter list (30%), and lexical proximity in the commit graph measured by shortest path in the parent-DAG (30%) to decide whether two symbols across a rename boundary should be linked; threshold defaults to 0.65 (calibrated against the codeshovel oracle dataset in tests/oracle_data/) but is exposed via --rename-threshold for users who want stricter or looser matching

src/embed/model.rs::build_context produces the string that gets fed to embed() — module path + symbol name + signature, sometimes with a brief doc-snippet, always truncated to the model's char_budget so the token-window isn't exceeded; the exact format is calibrated per-language (Rust uses fn name(args) -> ret with lifetimes elided, Python uses def name(args), TypeScript uses function name(args): ret, etc.) but the high-level pattern is consistent: 'where this symbol lives :: what it's called :: what shape it has', which empirically embeds better than just-the-name or just-the-body alone in the symbol-search task

src/cli/cmd_mcp.rs::install_for_agent installs vex as an MCP server for one of the supported agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Windsurf, Cline, Continue.dev, Zed) by writing the right JSON config file at the agent's expected path — each agent has a McpAgentHandler trait impl that knows its config file path, the JSON schema it expects, and how to atomically merge a new server entry without clobbering existing entries; adding a new agent ≈ 20 LOC handler + one JsonProfile const, see reference_mcp_install_arch

src/store/writer.rs::write_section_vectors L2-normalises every embedding before writing it into the dense vectors section, so search-time cosine reduces to a plain dot product (no per-query sqrt); the writer also tracks a global mean vector and writes it as a sidecar so future similarity-baseline experiments (rank by 'how different is this from the project average') don't require a re-embed pass — this was added in v1.13 P5 to fix a perf regression where every cosine call was paying for two sqrts

src/parse/typescript.rs::extract_typescript the TypeScript extractor handles both .ts and .tsx files via tree-sitter-typescript 0.23 with two grammars (typescript + tsx) selected by extension; captures function_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, type_alias_declaration, and enum_declaration nodes, plus arrow functions assigned to const / let bindings at module scope (heuristic: const Name = (...) => ... matches if Name is PascalCase OR the arrow body contains JSX); React component detection is best-effort and tagged via the modifier bitset for downstream filtering

src/embed/cache.rs::EmbeddingCache::get_or_insert two-tier cache: a hot in-memory LRU (configurable size, default 4096 entries) backed by a cold on-disk content-addressed store keyed by (embedder_id, sha256(context_string)); the disk store uses atomic rename for writes so concurrent vex processes against the same project don't corrupt each other's entries, and the embedder_id in the key means switching --embedder doesn't return stale vectors from the previous model; cache hits skip the ~80MB model load entirely if every symbol's context is already cached (see embedder_char_budget for the resolve-without-instantiating path)
